Evaluation

How we test it

Valio's booth told us what success means: when the delivery arrives, the kitchen can cook the whole menu, and the agent never commits to something a person should decide. Both evals below are graded by code, not by an LLM. A scorer written separately from the agent re-derives allergen violations from Valio's raw GS1 codes and re-checks availability through the API.

1 · Menu → cart

39 hand-written recipe cards (grams per portion, essential or not, allowed swaps), 124 gold ingredient rules over Valio's category codes, 10 dev cases + 6 held-out, including stock-outs and late deliveries. A dish is cookable if every essential component is bought at ≥ 80% of the gold quantity, arrives by the service date, and breaks no allergen rule.

2 · Request → commitment → approval

13 free-text buyer requests in the style of Valio's handout ("1,000 litres of lactose-free milk by Monday"), balanced between cases where the agent should act alone (7) and cases where it must stop (3 escalate, 3 refuse: a peanut order for a nut-free kitchen, every acceptable milk arriving late, a total salmon stock-out). Pass = right product, right quantity, on time, right approval call. pass^k means all k fresh runs pass.

What still fails

Fresh dill when it is out of stock, a few picks where our gold rules and the agent disagree (ham in an unusual category, burger patties for "mince"), and two quantities just under the 80% bar. A chef grades the disputed ones in eval/spot_checks.csv before any gold rule changes. Full ledger: eval/METRICS_LOG.md on GitHub.
